4. (Currently Amended) A method of impeding Leishmania transmission comprising administering to a human subject a composition comprising a Fucose Mannose Ligand (FML) fraction from Leishmania promastigotes or Leishmania amastigotes and saponin, wherein said FML fraction is derived from Leishmania species that cause human visceral leishmaniasis, and wherein the composition is formulated to induce blocking antibodies in humans at therapeutic concentrations capable of impeding transmission by sandfly vectors.

5. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 4, wherein said composition is in the form of a blocking vaccine formulated with saponin as an adjuvant to enhance immune response in humans.

6. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 4, wherein said composition further comprises suitable pharmaceutical vehicles, for blocking Leishmaniasis transmission in humans by reducing parasitemia levels and preventing transmission to sandfly vectors.

7. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 4, wherein the Leishmania promastigotes or Leishmania amastigotes fractions called "Fucose Mannose Ligand" (FML) comprise a glycoprotein complex containing 29% of neutral sugar, 44% of protein, 11% of phosphate and hexoamines traces composed by protein bands with molecular weight ranging from 9 to 95 kDa, some protein bands having carbohydrates at 36 and 54 to 68 kDa, the FML glycidic portion presenting 10% of fucose and 47% of mannose, 30% of glucose, 12% of galactose and xylose traces, amino acids containing 10 to 20% of glutamic acid, alanine, aspartic acid and glycine, 5 to 10% of serine, histidine, lysine, leucine, threonine, proline and valine, and 2 to 5% of arginine, methionine, isoleucine, tyrosine and phenylalanine, wherein said FML is specifically formulated and dosed to achieve blocking antibody titers in humans that are therapeutically effective at lower concentrations than those required in in vitro assays.
